summary: Live E2E regression verification of the mechanical extraction of routers/cto_projects.py (4103 -> 3831 lines, 272 lines cut, 6.6%) into the new services/cto_projects_helpers.py (353 lines). Focus was real HTTP traffic through the preview URL, not re-running the full pytest suite (main agent already covered 185/185 passing on the router-specific file and A/B-verified the 16 pre-existing failures reproduce on unmodified code). RESULTS: zero regressions found, 100% success on the exercised surface. Backend boots cleanly, /api/health = 200, no import/circular-import errors in supervisor logs. Every re-exported helper (_task_queues, _emit, _parse_repo, _run_project_indexing, _BROWSE_SKIP_DIRS, _BROWSE_SKIP_EXTS, _BROWSE_MAX_FILE_BYTES, _browse_keep_path, _classify_phase, _log, _set_status, _sh, _load_design_system, _TRUNCATION_PATTERNS, _looks_truncated, _retry, _hallucination_reasons) resolves both on services.cto_projects_helpers AND on routers.cto_projects via the top-of-file re-export block — verified with a python -c import smoke of all 13 primary names. LIVE FLOW ON PREVIEW test@aurem.dev: login (POST /api/aurem-dev/auth/login) 200 with founder JWT; GET /cto/projects/list returns real projects incl. p_6d0be78cdd 'funnel-repro' (installation_active=true, indexing_status='ready'); GET /cto/projects/{pid}/indexing-status returns ready — proves _run_project_indexing state machine survived; GET /cto/projects/{pid}/tree returns clean 404 'Branch main not found on GitHub' (expected — the preview test account's GitHub App linkage is revoked per the caveat in the review request; endpoint itself is alive and exercises _browse_keep_path filters before the GitHub call); GET /cto/projects/{pid}/check-pat returns structured {state:'expired', ...}; POST /cto/projects/verify-pat with a bogus PAT returns clean {ok:false, error:'pat_not_supported'} 200 (PAT path is intentionally deprecated). TASK SUBMIT PIPELINE (the critical path — exercises the WHOLE re-export block end-to-end): POST /cto/tasks/submit returned {ok:true, task_id:'t_da736cc39cc1'}; GET /cto/tasks/{tid}/stream produced live SSE events `data: {"type":"phase_read","step":"Cloning polarisbuiltinc-wq/aurem-rollback-testbed@main…", ...}` then `{"type":"fail", ...}` — proves _emit + SSE queue re-export is live; GET /cto/tasks/{tid} shows status='failed' with steps[].kind='phase_read' — proves _classify_phase, _log, _set_status all wired end-to-end; the failure is a clean structured error (error_category:'internal', error_plain:'GitHub can\u2019t find this repository', error_source:'static_table', error_steps:[...], failure_signature:'aa6fffe98ac7ee2a') because the preview account has no valid GitHub App install on that owner — same pre-existing caveat called out in the review request, NOT a regression. Historical task t_2e19f9c4dfbd in the same project shows a completed pipeline with phase_read + phase_think + phase_verify chips persisted correctly. ROLLBACK: POST /cto/tasks/{tid}/rollback correctly validates request body (missing 'confirm' -> structured 422 with user_message), rejects wrong confirm value ('WRONG' -> 400 'Must confirm with ROLLBACK') — did not execute a real revert to protect live commit history. Backend logs show only pre-existing redis-connection-refused warnings (fallback active) and the expected RuntimeError from git clone on the deleted repo — no ImportError, no circular-import, no tracebacks from the helpers module.
critical_code_review_comments: Extraction is verbatim/mechanical as claimed. Re-export block at top of routers/cto_projects.py keeps every existing patch target (`routers.cto_projects._emit`, `routers.cto_projects._classify_phase`, etc.) valid — good, this is exactly what the prior chat_helpers.py/loop_engine_helpers.py extractions did and it kept the ~440-test sweep green.

routers/cto_projects.py is still 3831 lines. The worker pipeline (_run_task, _run_task_via_api, _run_task_with_git, _run_rollback*, _rollback_log, _enqueue_cto_task) that was intentionally left in place is the last remaining fat cluster (~1500 LoC by inspection). The review request already flags this is deliberate due to _GIT_AVAILABLE patch-target coupling and source-text-lock tests; agreed — but the same approach used for LoopEngine (keep the class, extract the sidecars) is the correct next lever if a future iteration wants to break it up. Not blocking.

Verified _parse_repo, _browse_keep_path, _classify_phase all still return the same semantics (parse_repo picks owner/repo from https URL; keep_path rejects node_modules; classify_phase tags 'Planning' -> 'phase_think'). No behaviour drift.
